request.system: You are an experienced audio electronics technician diagnosing a unit on the bench. Exactly one component has failed. Use the measure tool to take readings (each costs effort; stay within the budget), then call diagnose with your ranked list of the most likely faults, naming them exactly as in the fault list. Think like a technician: compare readings with the healthy values and their tolerances.

messages.content:
Circuit: Block 3 - Passive Baxandall tone control. Passive Baxandall bass/treble control with 100k audio-taper pots at mid-rotation. About 27 dB mid-band insertion loss when driven from the triode stage's ~43k output impedance; within +1.3/-0.8 dB of the 1 kHz level from 20 Hz to 20 kHz at the centre settings.

Stages: tone = Passive tone control

Parts:
- R301: resistor 47k (stage tone)
- VR301: potentiometer 100k (stage tone)
- C301: film_cap 10n (stage tone)
- C302: film_cap 100n (stage tone)
- R302: resistor 4.7k (stage tone)
- R303: resistor 33k (stage tone)
- C303: film_cap 1n (stage tone)
- VR302: potentiometer 100k (stage tone)
- C304: film_cap 10n (stage tone)

Netlist of the healthy circuit (SPICE; node names as in the test points):
* Differential reference circuit - Block 3: passive Baxandall tone control (standalone)
* ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
* Original generic design written for this project, after the passive form of
* Baxandall's tone control (Wireless World, 1952). Bass: R301-VR301-R302 divider
* with C301/C302 bridging the pot sections. Treble: C303-VR302-C304 with the
* wiper to the output; the bass wiper joins the output through R303.
* Potentiometers are 100k audio (A) taper set to mid-rotation, which on an A
* taper leaves ~10 % of the track between wiper and the grounded end. Each pot
* is modelled as upper track (A), lower track (B) and a 1 ohm wiper contact (W).
* Fixtures: source with 43k output impedance (the triode stage's Ra || rp) and a
* 100k load (the op-amp stage bias resistor).
* Run standalone: ngspice -b circuits/tone/tone.cir
* ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
.include ../lib/devices.lib

* ---- Fixtures ----
VIN_T tone_src 0 DC 0 AC 1 SIN(0 1 1k)
RSRC_T tone_src tone_in 43k
RLOAD_OP tone_out 0 100k

* ---- Bass section ----
R301 tone_in bass_a 47k
RVR301A bass_a bass_t 90k
RVR301B bass_t bass_b 10k
RVR301W bass_t bass_w 1
C301 bass_a bass_w 10n
C302 bass_w bass_b 100n
R302 bass_b 0 4.7k
R303 bass_w tone_out 33k

* ---- Treble section ----
C303 tone_in treb_a 1n
RVR302A treb_a treb_t 90k
RVR302B treb_t treb_b 10k
RVR302W treb_t tone_out 1
C304 treb_b 0 10n

.control
set noaskquit
ac dec 5 10 100k
let gdb = db(mag(v(tone_out)))
print gdb
.endc
.end

Test points:
- TP10: node tone_in, Tone-control input (stage tone)
- TP11: node bass_w, Bass control wiper (stage tone)
- TP12: node tone_out, Tone-control output (stage tone)

Measurements (key | what | healthy reading and range | cost):
- dc:TP10 | DC voltage at TP10 | 0 µV (range -822 µV to 822 µV) | cost 1
- dc:TP11 | DC voltage at TP11 | 0 µV (range -822 µV to 822 µV) | cost 1
- dc:TP12 | DC voltage at TP12 | 0 µV (range -822 µV to 822 µV) | cost 1
- ac:TP10 | 1 kHz signal level (gain from input) at TP10 | 0.539 V/V (-5.4 dB) (range 0.509 V/V (-5.9 dB) to 0.571 V/V (-4.9 dB)) | cost 3
- ac:TP11 | 1 kHz signal level (gain from input) at TP11 | 0.0485 V/V (-26.3 dB) (range 0.0449 V/V (-27.0 dB) to 0.0525 V/V (-25.6 dB)) | cost 3
- ac:TP12 | 1 kHz signal level (gain from input) at TP12 | 0.0449 V/V (-27.0 dB) (range 0.0415 V/V (-27.6 dB) to 0.0486 V/V (-26.3 dB)) | cost 3
- ac20:TP12 | 20 Hz response (gain from input) at TP12 | 0.0509 V/V (-25.9 dB) (range 0.0409 V/V (-27.8 dB) to 0.0633 V/V (-24.0 dB)) | cost 3
- ac20k:TP12 | 20 kHz response (gain from input) at TP12 | 0.0406 V/V (-27.8 dB) (range 0.0313 V/V (-30.1 dB) to 0.0527 V/V (-25.6 dB)) | cost 3
- lift:<ref> | desolder one lead of a part and test it out of circuit | result: within or out of tolerance | cost 10 (12 for parts on high-voltage nodes)

Fault list (name faults exactly like this):
- R301:open: R301 open circuit
- R301:short: R301 short circuit
- R301:drift_x0.5: R301 value drifted to 0.5x
- R301:drift_x2: R301 value drifted to 2x
- R301:drift_x10: R301 value drifted to 10x
- VR301:wiper_open: VR301 wiper open
- VR301:track_open: VR301 track open
- C301:open: C301 open circuit
- C301:short: C301 short circuit
- C302:open: C302 open circuit
- C302:short: C302 short circuit
- R302:open: R302 open circuit
- R302:short: R302 short circuit
- R302:drift_x0.5: R302 value drifted to 0.5x
- R302:drift_x2: R302 value drifted to 2x
- R302:drift_x10: R302 value drifted to 10x
- R303:open: R303 open circuit
- R303:short: R303 short circuit
- R303:drift_x0.5: R303 value drifted to 0.5x
- R303:drift_x2: R303 value drifted to 2x
- R303:drift_x10: R303 value drifted to 10x
- C303:open: C303 open circuit
- C303:short: C303 short circuit
- VR302:wiper_open: VR302 wiper open
- VR302:track_open: VR302 track open
- C304:open: C304 open circuit
- C304:short: C304 short circuit

Budget: 40 effort units.

Customer complaint: We've got a channel strip in the control room that's been playing up. Vocals come through weak and we're running out of gain. We were told the internal voltages around one of the stages are out of spec. It sounds thin, there's no weight in the low end anymore. It's only slight, but it's there. Thanks for taking a look.

Diagnose the unit. (Session 2 of 3.)

content.text: I'll start with the AC levels at the three test points and the DC at the input.

content.thinking: TP12 is low at 1 kHz and much lower at 20 Hz (-37 dB against a healthy -25.9 dB), while TP11 and the input at TP10 are normal. The fault lies between the bass wiper and the output, or in the treble branch, so I'm checking the high-end response and DC levels next.
The 20 kHz level is normal while the 20 Hz level is down about 11 dB, so the fault is bass-specific among C301, C302, R302 and R303. I'm lifting C302 first to check TP11 at 20 Hz.

content.text: C302 tests good out of circuit, which rules out C302 open. Spending 10 on another lift is affordable, so I'll try C301.

tools.name: diagnose
tools.description: Finish with a ranked list of fault names.

content.thinking: The budget is nearly gone, so I'm ranking the leftover bass candidates: C301, C302, then R302, R303 and VR301. R302 drifting high best explains the selective bass loss, since R303 would also reduce 20 kHz.
